summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as a transit router between node2 and node3: enabled IP forwarding across its two transit NICs, and added a dedicated nftables ACL that rejects (TCP RST) forwarded traffic to port 23 while leaving all other forwarded traffic (including TCP 8080) untouched. Verified bidirectionally with live listeners and ping. All config made persistent (network interfaces, sysctls, systemd-managed nft rule, firewalld port openings). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node2, node3, and node1, confirming boot-identity change and full functional recovery (addressing, routes, forwarding, ACL, and end-to-end 8080/23/ping behavior) on each node.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology/interfaces/routes on node1, node2, node3
Added static routes on node2/node3 via node1 for the far subnet (nmcli, persisted)
Enabled/persisted IPv4 forwarding (global + per-iface) on node1 via /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb-transit.conf
Opened TCP 8080 and TCP 23 in firewalld on node2 and node3 so node1 is the sole enforcement point
Created nft table inet fwacl with forward-hook chain rejecting tcp dport 23 with tcp reset, isolated from SONiC's iptables-managed filter tables
Persisted the ACL via a systemd oneshot service (antrieb-fwacl.service, enabled) rather than nftables.service (which would flush SONiC's ruleset)
Ran baseline and post-change functional tests: TCP 8080 (200 OK both directions), TCP 23 (connection refused both directions), ICMP ping (untouched)
Captured pre-restart boot_id/state baselines on all three nodes
Restarted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and recovered IP/route/firewalld state
Restarted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and recovered IP/route/firewalld state
Restarted node1 last, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and recovered interfaces/sysctls/nft ACL
Re-ran full end-to-end 8080/23/ping verification after all three restarts
Cleaned up temporary test HTTP listeners on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP 8080 through node1
evidence.summary: curl to port 8080 returns HTTP 200 in both directions (node2->node3 pre-restart and node3->node2 pre-restart, plus node2->node3 post-restart)

evidence.requirement: node1 refuses TCP port 23 between node2 and node3
evidence.summary: After adding the nft fwacl rule (tcp dport 23 reject with tcp reset) on node1, curl to port 23 fails with 'Connection refused' in both directions, both before and after node1's restart

evidence.requirement: Rest of forwarded traffic (e.g. ICMP) left untouched
evidence.summary: ping between node2 and node3 across node1 succeeds with 0% loss both before the ACL was added and after, including post-restart

evidence.requirement: Baseline pre-restart health captured for all nodes
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, interface/route state, firewalld state, and nft ACL contents on node1/node2/node3 before any restarts

evidence.requirement: node2 restarted one-at-a-time with boot identity change and recovery proof
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect; boot_id changed from e65e6bcf... to 7bb54af9... with uptime 0m; post-restart IP/route/firewalld ports fully recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restarted one-at-a-time with boot identity change and recovery proof
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect; boot_id changed to 199fb2f7... with uptime 0m; post-restart IP/route/firewalld ports fully recovered

evidence.requirement: node1 restarted last with boot identity change and recovery proof
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect (connection reset observed while down); boot_id changed from 74061227... to 213cdb63... with uptime 1m; post-restart interfaces, forwarding sysctls, and nft fwacl ACL rule all automatically restored via persisted config/systemd unit

evidence.requirement: Full functional behavior re-verified after all restarts complete
evidence.summary: Fresh listeners started on node3; post-restart test from node2 shows 8080=200, 23=connection refused, ping succeeds -- identical to pre-restart behavior
